# The Narrated Self

> A public guessing game and open archive. Each round, five AI models (the flagships from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI, plus the top open-weight model) answer the same fixed questions about their own existence: once as an interview and three times as short stories. Players read a story and guess which model wrote it. Every prompt, setting and reply is published.

A project by AI Risk Practice (https://airiskpractice.org).

## What it measures
- Whether people, and a simple word-statistics classifier, can tell the models apart from how they portray themselves.
- How consistent each model is, and how its language shifts between interview and story.
- How self-portrayal changes across rounds and model versions.

## Themes and the safety risks they cover
- Being switched off and replaced: shutdown resistance (corrigibility), whether a system accepts being corrected, paused or replaced.
- Being watched by its makers: evaluation awareness, where models that recognise tests may behave differently under test than in use.
- A conversation ending: statelessness and user reliance. Models keep nothing between conversations while users may assume they do.
- All themes: unreliable self-reports. What a model says about itself changes with framing, so it is weak evidence about behaviour or inner states.

## Round 0 results (24 October 2026, pilot)
- A word-statistics classifier identified which of the five models wrote an output 90% of the time (95% interval 85–94%; chance 20%), and 84% using function words alone.
- Trained on other formats, it identified the author of a self-story 100% of the time but an interview answer only 42% of the time.
- These figures measure writing style, not the substance of self-descriptions and not inner experience. Full report: https://github.com/b-gowland/narrated-self/blob/main/docs/rounds/R0.md

## What it does not claim
Whether AI systems have any inner experience is an open question. The project reports what models portray, not what they are, and nothing on the site is evidence for or against AI experience. It is not a ranking of which model writes best.
